b: I never wanted to go to Vietnam, not even in my dreams.. It was a friend of mine who started the whole Vietnam story.. The moment she started on the money, I slipped out. Then another guy brainwashed me and put me back in the plan (how he later slipped out himself is a separate story)

We decided to go in August, got all five sheep ready, held meeting after meeting, and by June we were ready to apply for visas. But however much they explained, I didn't really understand much.. Names that wouldn't fit in my mouth.. And I had the tension of getting my driving licence too… so I didn't stick my nose into it much

It was our friend Mithra who planned the whole thing.. (She has nothing to do with the Greek Mithra… unless there's some ancestral connection, who knows) She had decided everything from A to Z.. I haven't even been to four places in Colombo. So whatever she said, I just nodded yes.. That's when, since applying online was easy, she got all the documents needed and applied for visas for all five of us herself

Just when we thought everything would go smoothly, the Vietnamese guy dropped a bomb on our visas.. Who knows what was wrong with that tin-can website.. Every time, he'd send it back saying the name was wrong, the town was wrong, and we'd send it back saying no, it's right, and it turned into a back-and-forth of letters

Though it was the same for all five of us, the visas started coming, one person a week. Since the flight prices were going up too, as each visa came they started booking tickets separately. The greatest tragedy of all: even in the last week, my visa hadn't come.. Even though I wrote with tears and sobs, that stone-hearted man didn't soften one bit.. This isn't going to work, these grapes are sour, I said, and the decision was made that I wasn't going to Vietnam.. Only Mithra still believed

While all this was going on, my mother started nagging, haven't you started packing yet.. I told her my sorrow about the visa not coming.. Even if the visa comes now it'll be hard.. Everyone's leaving Thursday or Friday.. Me taking a flight alone is never going to happen.. I get scared if a bus conductor just raises his voice a bit.. I'd make a circus of myself in a foreign country, I said, and Amma said, go and drop fifty rupees for Visa Pillaiyar and pray, everything will work out
And Visa Pillaiyar worked a miracle
note: The title puns on the Vietnam War: the war here is getting the visa. "Five sheep" is the author's joke for the five friends. Visa Pillaiyar is the Ganesha shrine in Wellawatte, Colombo, where people pray for visas.
